title: Assessment and Diagnosis in Children and Adolescents
welcome: A good assessment is an act of respect: it tells a child, what is happening to you has a name, and a path. This course teaches you to see clearly and name carefully.
vignette: Two clinicians watch the same restless nine-year-old. One sees ADHD; the other sees anxiety; a third sees a sleepless home. Only careful, multi-source assessment can tell which story is true, and the child's next years depend on it.
vignette_attr: A diagnostic conference, drawn from practice
description: A comprehensive course in assessment and diagnosis with young people: the DSM-5-TR and ICD-11 disorders of childhood and adolescence, the assessment interview, behavioral observation, rating scales and testing basics, differential diagnosis, and writing clear, humane reports.
questions: What is the difference between a symptom and a signal?
How do I hold multiple informants who disagree?
How do I write a diagnosis that opens doors rather than closing them?
importance: Misdiagnosis redirects a childhood; careful diagnosis rescues it
Assessment skill is required for referral, treatment, and advocacy
Reports are legal and clinical documents; they must be excellent
misconceptions: that diagnosis labels and harms, when careful diagnosis protects and guides
that rating scales diagnose, when they only inform a clinical judgment
figures: whose empirical assessment system standardized child measurement
who advanced structured child psychiatric assessment
outcomes: Apply DSM-5-TR and ICD-11 to youth

integration: Assessment anchors treatment planning across every clinical course in this programme.
faith: We name carefully because every name is carried by a soul made in the image of God.
closing: May your eyes be precise and your words be kind, and may your reports open every right door.
